# Entries permitted at the repository root -- files and directories alike, one
# per line, no trailing slash on directories.
#
# Every entry here is deliberate. The root is where scratch artefacts land,
# because `git add -A` in a worktree you have been working in does not care what
# a file is for, and a one-line addition at the root is invisible in a large
# diff. Seven entries have reached `main` this way, in six incidents. The list
# was built by walking every root path ever added on main and subtracting what
# is still here -- not by collecting the ones somebody reported:
#
#   .msg.txt       39675330b -> bbc193117    1.6h
#   .commitmsg/    faedea4d1 -> 490b846c3      3m   <- DIRECTORIES, one incident,
#   .goldens/      faedea4d1 -> 490b846c3      3m      removed by "Remove
#                                                      accidentally tracked PR
#                                                      artifacts"
#   .wa64.log      83a51bfa6 -> c07acaa78   17.2h
#   .commitmsg     e42fa9470 -> 398cff8e5   19.8h   (#1881, removed by #1999)
#   .pris_v4.log   589d48ffd -> 7a6482c83    1.3h   (#1951, removed by #1975)
#   .body.md       79196f89d -> 54625db9d    2.7h   (#2026, removed by #2036)
#
# Excluded, because their removal commits say what they were: `site` (moved to
# onnx-genai-wiki, #1488), `third_party` (oneDNN backend removal) and
# `abresults` (a `docs(benchmarks):` commit recording a result, reconsidered
# 5.5 days later -- intentional when added, which is what separates it).
#
# Each was repaired by adding one more pattern to .gitignore, and each time the
# next one was named outside every pattern. .body.md landed *after* two such
# fixes, hours after both, and the name it should have had (.pr-body.md) was
# already ignored. Enumerating what belongs is the only form of this check that
# does not need to predict the next name.
#
# Directories are listed because two of the seven are directories, and a check
# comparing only files cannot see one: `.commitmsg/m.txt` contains a separator,
# so a files-only filter discards it as "not at the root". #2036 shipped that
# gap while citing that very instance in its own header.
#
# To add a root entry legitimately: add it here in the same PR. That is the
# escape hatch, and unlike a label it leaves a permanent record of the decision.
